title: Make opposition strong enough to reveal the choice.
dek: In Chapter 17 of Story, Robert McKee shows why the forces opposing a desire must be strong enough to expose what the protagonist truly wants and what the choice will cost.

meta.canon: Robert McKee, Story: Substance, Structure, Style, and the Principles of Screenwriting

marginNote.label: Apprenticeship Note
marginNote.body: A desire becomes dramatically legible only when something capable of defeating it stands in the way. Weak opposition produces easy outcomes; strong opposition makes the choice reveal the person and the price of the result.

canon.heading: Make opposition strong enough to reveal the choice.
canon.standfirst: Read the opening section of Chapter 17, "The Principle of Antagonism," from Robert McKee's Story on PDF pages 389-408. Study how credible opposition tests desire and makes consequence visible, then stop at PDF page 408.
canon.readerIntro: Read this section as a study of dramatic pressure. Mark how the opposing force is sized against the protagonist's desire, where conflict moves from obstacle to meaningful choice, and what the cost of pursuit reveals. Then map one narrative or offer: name the desire, the strongest force against it, the choice under pressure, and the consequence. Stop at PDF page 408.

blocks.label: 01 / Give desire a force that can defeat it
paragraphs: McKee treats antagonism as the force that makes desire consequential rather than decorative.
Notice whether the opposition can genuinely block, redirect, or expose the goal—not merely delay it.

blocks.label: 02 / Escalate pressure through incompatible forces
paragraphs: Strong conflict comes from forces whose goals, values, or needs cannot all be satisfied at once.
Mark the turns where a simple obstacle becomes a choice between meaningful losses.

blocks.label: 03 / Let opposition reveal character
paragraphs: A protagonist's response to capable opposition exposes priorities more clearly than a stated self-description.
Separate what the character says they value from what the pressured choice makes them protect or sacrifice.

blocks.label: 04 / Map one consequential conflict
paragraphs: Choose one story, pitch, or customer decision. Write the desire, opposing force, forced choice, and irreversible consequence in four lines.
Strengthen the opposition until the choice teaches the audience something they could not learn from an easy win.

closeReading: What makes an opposing force strong enough to threaten the protagonist's actual desire?
Where does the chapter distinguish a meaningful antagonistic force from a merely convenient obstacle?
How do incompatible values or needs turn pressure into a consequential choice?
What does the protagonist's response to opposition reveal that their stated identity does not?
How would you strengthen the opposition in one customer or brand narrative without making the conflict artificial?

principle.heading: Make the choice expensive enough to mean something.
principle.body: A narrative becomes persuasive when the desired outcome must survive a force capable of changing it; the cost of the choice is the evidence that the result matters.
principle.example: A product story does not stop at a customer wanting efficiency. It shows the customer choosing a new workflow despite a real switching cost, then living with a measurable result that proves the change.
principle.practice: Choose one narrative or offer. Name the protagonist's desire, the strongest credible force against it, the choice pressure creates, and the consequence. Remove any obstacle that cannot change the decision.

output.heading: Make the opposition carry the proof.
output.body: When the force against a desire is credible, the choice becomes legible and the consequence earns belief.

signals.heading: Four current signals on making capability, attention, and consequence visible.

fieldNotes.title: Anthropic makes model capability compete on cost and inspectability
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, describing gains in coding, reasoning, vision, speed, and safety evaluation. It says the models generate outputs up to 30% faster, cost less than the prior versions, and include a fast mode at a higher price.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The product is not asking capability to stand alone as proof. It pairs stronger performance with speed, price, and visible safety evidence, giving buyers several concrete reasons to choose the new model over a familiar incumbent.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether customers can reproduce the claimed task-level gains in their own workflows, or whether benchmark and launch language remains stronger than the operational evidence.

fieldNotes.title: Medium puts AI inside the writing decision, not beside it
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Medium launched TK, a private notebook app intended to help ideas compound into finished writing. The product combines a writing space with importing, mobile capture, social sharing, and AI assistance that can work with a writer's existing material.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The meaningful opposition is the blank page and the scattered archive, not a lack of another chat window. By placing assistance inside the writing loop, Medium gives the product a chance to change behavior at the moment a thought would otherwise be abandoned.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether TK increases finished, revisited work rather than merely increasing drafts, prompts, and AI-generated text.

fieldNotes.title: YouTube and Billboard revise the rule that decides whose listening counts
fieldNotes.whatHappened: YouTube said its streaming data will return to the U.S. Billboard charts in 2027 after Billboard changed its methodology to narrow the gap between subscription-supported and ad-supported streams. YouTube had stopped supplying data in January 2026.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: A measurement system is also a story about what matters. Changing the conversion rule changes which audience behavior becomes visible, which artists receive credit, and which strategies look successful to the market.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch how the revised weighting changes the ranking of artists with large free, international, or video-first audiences, and whether the new measure better matches actual discovery behavior.

fieldNotes.title: Pepsi extends one food story across holiday media and retail
fieldNotes.whatHappened: Pepsi expanded its 'Food Deserves Pepsi' platform into holiday and football campaigns, including a Santa spot, Walmart creative, fan experiences, and a reported 80% increase in retail visibility over the year-ago period.
fieldNotes.whyItMatters: The campaign gives the brand a repeatable opposition: moments when food could be paired with something else. The creative becomes stronger because the same choice is reinforced across culture, media, and the shelf instead of being left to one memorable ad.
fieldNotes.watch: Watch whether the expanded presence increases Pepsi's association with food occasions and purchase, or only increases exposure without changing the choice at the point of sale.

tweets.title: A startup wins when the new physics force a new story
tweets.summary: This is worth keeping because it treats narrative as part of the operating system, not decoration. A strange technical or market bet has to become desirable before incumbents copy it, and the company has to keep moving fast enough that the story remains attached to real progress.
